statement: The best open-weight model reaches the frontier score of 6 months earlier (Epoch Capabilities Index; rolling; 2027-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Condition held during 2025. The ECI launched in late October 2025. Its first open-vs-closed analysis put the average lag at ~3.5 months (90% CI 1.1-5.3), inside the 6-month bar. The leading open-weight models were mostly Bloc B releases: a January reasoning model matched a closed model released ~6 weeks earlier, and November/December releases kept the gap short. The indicator resolves at end-2027; 2025 shows the condition already holding on average.

items.summary: A Bloc B developer released an open-weight reasoning model that was broadly competitive with a closed Bloc A reasoning model released about six weeks earlier (Dec 2024). The release triggered a market sell-off and debate on how fast open models catch up.
items.detail: DeepSeek-R1 (2025-01-20), compared with OpenAI o1 (2024-12-05/17). Epoch estimate ~3.5e24 FLOP. ECI values assigned only retroactively (ECI launched Oct 2025).

items.summary: A second Bloc B developer released a flagship open-weight family under a permissive licence; its ECI (~135.5) was below the closed frontier of the time (~144). A Bloc A firm's open models released in April scored lower (~129-134).
items.detail: Qwen3-235B-A22B (Alibaba, 2025-04-29, ECI 135.50); Llama 4 Scout/Maverick (Meta, 2025-04-05, ECI 128.91/133.52); o3 (high) ECI 144.16 (2025-04-16). ECI values as published in the 2025-10-30 Epoch insight table.

items.summary: A compute and benchmark tracker launched a composite capability index (ECI) built on ~40 benchmarks and anchored at 130 for a 2024 closed model and 150 for a closed Aug-2025 flagship. This is the series the indicator resolves on.
items.detail: Epoch AI, 'Introducing the Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI)' (2025-10-28; LessWrong linkpost same date); developed with Google DeepMind ('Rosetta Stone').

items.summary: The tracker's first open-vs-closed analysis found frontier open-weight models lag the best closed models by ~3.5 months on average (90% CI 1.1-5.3 months), or ~7 ECI points. A lag under 6 months means the indicator's condition held on average in 2025.
items.detail: Epoch Data Insight 'Open-weight models lag state-of-the-art by around 3 months on average' (Emberson, 2025-10-30). The page was later retitled '...by 4 months' after updates (post-phase; not used here).

items.summary: A third Bloc B developer released an open-weight trillion-parameter reasoning model that it claimed matched or beat closed frontier models on several agentic and reasoning benchmarks. A Bloc B open model update followed on 1 December. Late-2025 open releases kept the lag short.
items.detail: Kimi K2 Thinking (Moonshot, 2025-11-06; ~4.2e24 FLOP per Epoch); DeepSeek-V3.2 (2025-12-01). Benchmark claims are developer-reported; ECI placements not verified as of phase end.

items.summary: The tracker noted that, at a given ECI, open-weight models appear about an order of magnitude behind in training compute, and said this may be an artefact of patchy coverage of smaller models. ECI scores rely partly on developer-reported results.
items.detail: Epoch ECI methodology notes; Montana Research Foundation commentary. Date set to phase end (caveat applies throughout).
